newsitem.title: FRANCE: New French spending by July decree, to be neutral.
newsitem.headline: New French spending by July decree, to be neutral.

text.p: New spending measures announced by French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin in his parliamentary policy speech last week will be implemented by decrees to be published in July, a finance ministry source said on Wednesday.

The spending, including a quadrupling of "back-to-school" payments to families with children in education are expected to cost around 10 billion francs, but other public spending credits will be "redeployed" to compensate, the source said.
"There will be a redeployment of credits so as not to increase spending," said the source. "That's the policy."
The July decrees will be followed by a mini-budget after the summer recess as well as preparation of the 1998 budget law, to be debated in the National Assembly in November, the source said.

The government is currently awaiting the outcome of an audit of public finances to be presented by the auditors on July 21 and, according to Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn on Tuesday, the results will be made public "immediately".

Liberation newspaper said on Wednesday that Strauss-Kahn had told Socialist members of parliament in a closed-door meeting that the public deficit in 1997 was expected to come in between 3.6 and 3.8 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
The finance ministry declined to comment on the report.

Strauss-Kahn is due to speak to the National Assembly's influential finance committee on Wednesday of next week at 1000 GMT and to the committee's counterpart in the Senate, the upper house of parliament, on Thursday of next week at 1000 GMT.
